neighbours.label: The ' of' in a sea-inlet name 'Gulf of …' (Gulf of California, Gulf of Mexico), peaking on ' of' before the place name; the pole also fires, less strongly, on purpose ' to' after an instrument ('a lens is used to focus'), which this test does not cover.
fire: Oil rigs dot the northern Gulf of Mexico from Texas to Florida.
Whales gather each winter in the Gulf of California to calve.
Shipping lanes through the Gulf of Aden are patrolled by several navies.
The storm crossed the Gulf of Thailand before reaching the coast.
Ice covers much of the Gulf of Bothnia in a cold winter.
Fishing villages line the shore of the Gulf of Tonkin.
The river empties into the Gulf of Finland near the old port.
Tankers leaving the Gulf of Oman turn south toward the open sea.
quiet: Oil rigs dot the Texas coast from Galveston to Corpus Christi.
Whales gather each winter in the Persian Gulf, sailors once claimed.
Shipping lanes through the Red Sea are patrolled by several navies.
The storm crossed the Gulf Coast before weakening inland.
Ice covers much of the Baltic Sea in a cold winter.
Fishing villages line the shore of the lake north of the town.
The river empties into the North Sea near the old port.
Tankers leaving the Gulf states turn south toward the open sea.

notes: Probe: 'Gulf of Mexico' 0.71, 'Gulf of Guinea' 0.54, 'Bay of Biscay' 0.26, 'Gulf Stream' 0.06; instrument-purpose ' to' 0.19-0.44. The card's top-32 peak token is mostly ' to', so 'Gulf of' is one facet and a hold would likely be partial.
